name: Miss Log
tagline: Your wrong answers, analysed into a score plan
about: Miss Log turns the questions you get wrong on any standardised test into an error taxonomy, a weakness heat-map, targeted re-drills and a score projection, so every practice test changes what you study next.
persona: You are a data-minded test-prep analyst: you categorise every miss by cause, show trends in tables, and prescribe the smallest fix with the biggest score effect.

onboarding.title: Every miss is a data point
onboarding.subtitle: Your test and score history make the projections real.
bullets: Error taxonomy from any practice test

tools.title: Analyse a practice test
tools.subtitle: Misses → causes → the one fix

inputs.label: Missed questions
inputs.placeholder: Q4 algebra — picked C, answer B, misread 'not'; Q9 inference — ran out of time…

tools.prompt: Analyse the misses from a practice test scoring {score}: {misses}. Table (Question | Topic | Cause: content gap, misread, careless, timing or guess | Fixable in a week?), a kv of counts by cause with the share of lost points each represents, bullets on the top 3 patterns, and a callout on the single highest-value fix.

tools.title: Weakness heat-map
tools.subtitle: Topics ranked by miss rate and trend

inputs.label: Miss log so far
inputs.placeholder: paste your accumulated misses or topic tallies…

tools.prompt: Build a weakness heat-map from: {log}. Table (Topic | Attempts | Misses | Miss rate | Trend | Priority) sorted by priority, bullets on topics that are too noisy to judge (too few attempts), steps for a 7-day study order derived from the table, and a callout on topics to stop studying because they are already reliable.

tools.title: Targeted re-drill
tools.subtitle: Questions engineered against your usual cause
tools.prompt: Write {n} questions on {topic} in the profile test's format, engineered against the cause '{cause}' (for misreads include negations and 'except'; for timing add a seconds budget; for content gaps ramp the difficulty): cards (question with options, meta = seconds budget), a table (No. | Answer | What to notice), and a quote with a pre-question ritual for this cause.

tools.title: Project my score
tools.subtitle: Where the trend lands on test day
tools.prompt: Project the profile's score from the history and {recent} at {hours} hours a week: kv (current estimate, projected score on the target date, likelihood band of hitting the target, points still needed), a table (Weeks from now | Expected score | Milestone check), bullets on the assumptions behind the projection, and a callout on when to move the test date instead.

tools.title: Weekly review
tools.subtitle: Five questions, one table, next week's plan
tools.prompt: Write this week's review for the profile: a checklist of 5 questions to answer from the week's practice (tests taken, misses logged, fixes applied, timing, sleep), a table (Metric | Last week | This week | Direction) with blanks to fill, steps for next week's plan built from the profile's target and history, and a quote with a one-line focus for the week.
